title.narrative: Emergency response to population affected by floods in Maban County.

description.narrative: This project responds to the humanitarian needs among the population affected by flash floods in Bunj centre of Maban County in Upper Nile. The focus of the project is to distribute water treatment tablets to households so that they can have access to safe water, distribute non-food items, repair boreholes and supply essential medicine to the population in Bunj County. The project will be implemented by CAFOD together with Sudanaid staff based in Maban County. The water treatment tablets and majority of the NFIs would be provided by UNICEF, whereas CAFOD will purchase medicine and transport the, to Maban County. In addition, CAFOD will provide some first line non-food items mainly the impregnated mosquito-nets, and plastic sheeting to provide temporary shelter to the households who lost their huts. The water purification tablets will target all households affected by floods. The mosquito-nets and plastic sheeting will be distributed to vulnerable groups such as female headed households, pregnant women or those with children under the age of 5 and disabled household heads. The medicine will be given to the health unit in Jamam so that the population will have proper treatment. CAFOD and Sudanaid will also increase the number of hygiene sessions among the affected population. CAFOD and Sudanaid are part of an emergency response team formed in Maban County. The team consists of Medair, Relief International, and Serving in Mission, the South Sudan Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (SSRRC) and UN agencies. The team has been monitoring the floods situation in Maban since early September when 311 households were affected until recent assessment which reported that about 7500 households are affected and need urgent support. The main needs identified are water and sanitation, health and food. World Food Programme will provide food for distribution.UNICEF will provide water purification tablets and NFIs for distribution and CAFOD together with Sudanaid will take the lead in this sector because of their previous involvement in water and sanitation and NFIs distribution. The project will demonstrate international humanitarian community’s solidarity to the recently resettled population of Maban especially at this critical moment when the returning population is finding itself in areas with very limited basic services. Some of the returnees are reported to have returned to their pervious areas of refugee or displacement because of lack of infrastructure and services in their areas of origin.
